result.topic_en: Riemann distinguishes the 'listening' from the 'non-listening' ear by the stapes footplate being pressed slightly against the labyrinth fluid through the pull of the tensor tympani, and argues against objections to a continuous tension of the ossicular apparatus.

items.english: We make the distinction between the listening and the non-listening ear according to whether the stapes footplate is pressed slightly against the labyrinth water by the pull of the tensor tympani muscle, so that the pressure in the labyrinth water is slightly greater than in the air of the tympanic cavity.

items.english: In doing so, the parts of the solid bodies whose contact is to be secured are pressed slightly against one another.

items.english: Those who consider such a continuous tension of the apparatus (perhaps excepting the eardrum) improbable may assume that, with temperature changes, the ossicles change their position through the action of the suspensory and joint ligaments and the gradual change in the contraction of the muscles, without being pressed against one another.
